article.linkText: Bulls beat Cavaliers 122-108 behind Jordan Hawkins' 19 points and 63 off the bench
article.story: CHICAGO -- — Jordan Hawkins scored a season-high 19 points, Buddy Hield had 17 and the Chicago Bulls got 63 points off the bench as they held on to beat the Cleveland Cavaliers 122-108 on Monday night. Matas Buzelis added 15 points — all in the first half — as Bulls coach Tiago Splitter spread out playing time after a 151-145 overtime loss to Denver on Sunday. Tre Jones finished with 16 points and nine assists as six Bulls players reached double figures. Chicago shot 45.8% from the field and hit 20 of 49 from 3-point range. Donovan Mitchell led the Cavs with 28 points and James Harden added 21 after the 37-year-old guard scored 51 in their previous game, a 128-119 win over Indiana on Friday. The Bulls put it away with a strong fourth quarter, including a 10-0 spurt capped by Josh Giddey's finger-roll layup 4:23 in that made it 113-97. Jones hit a quirky 3 with 3:56 to go to make it 120-104. Giddey was limited to four points, 11 assists and two rebounds in 22 minutes after posting 23 points, 14 rebounds and a career-high 22 assists on Sunday. Chicago was clinging to a 93-89 lead entering the fourth quarter after building a 24-point cushion with a big second quarter, when it outscored Cleveland 45-20. The Bulls led 72-50 at halftime. The score was tied 32-all a minute into the second period when the Bulls got hot — buoyed by their bench — while the Cavs went cold. Chicago opened the lead to 24 using a series of runs, including a 12-2 spurt. Chicago shot 49% in the half and hit 11 of 25 from long distance, with Buzelis nailing four 3s. The Cavs responded immediately in the third quarter, starting with a 9-0 run. They outscored Chicago 39-21 in the period to trim it to 93-89 on Mitchell's driving layup with 2 seconds left. Up next Cavaliers: At the New York Knicks on Wednesday. Bulls: At Charlotte on Wednesday. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here
